_note: Static country-level markers for networks with no physical station pins. Consumed by index.html alongside stations.json. THIS FILE IS USER-FACING: every `note` and `yearly_cost` string renders directly in map popup tooltips for hobbyists. See `_note_field_convention` and `_yearly_cost_convention` below before editing.
_note_field_convention: The popup auto-renders the access label, yearly_cost, region, note, and registration URL — so `note` should ADD information beyond those, not restate them. DO NOT: repeat the price (it's in yearly_cost), repeat the access label ('Paid subscription required' is already shown), restate the region, include the registration URL inline (it renders separately), or instruct the user to 'contact X' (link to the website via `registration` instead). DO include, when applicable: station count once ('78 stations'), free hobbyist alternatives ('Volunteer rtk2go/Centipede bases provide partial free coverage'), terminal access blockers in plain words, real safety/operational warnings, non-obvious access mechanics. Tone: matter-of-fact, hobbyist-addressed, ≤2 short sentences typical, ~250 chars max. Skip the field entirely if there's nothing useful to add.
_yearly_cost_convention: Single short line, one of: '$X/yr' (USD), '€X/yr (~$Y/yr)' / '£X/yr' / '¥X/yr' / '₹X/yr' / '₽X/yr' / 'S$X/yr' (symbol currencies), or 'X CCY/yr (~$Y/yr)' for ISO-only codes (CHF, SEK, NOK, RSD, etc.). Drop the '~' prefix unless the figure is genuinely uncertain (estimates are implicit). If pricing is not published, OMIT the field entirely so the line disappears from the popup — do not write 'pricing not publicly listed' there. Multi-tier pricing: lead with the primary tier; mention any hobbyist-relevant secondary tier in `note`. Local-currency qualifiers (e.g. 'private users only') belong in `note`, not `yearly_cost`.
_tiers: Five values describing the network's nature from a hobbyist's perspective: 'free' (no fee to use; coloured circle if in-pipeline + has data, grey circle otherwise; note must truthfully open with 'N stations, free.' when no data is ingested yet); 'paid' (commercial subscription, hobbyist can buy access; circled-? marker; yearly_cost recommended); 'paid-affordable' (paid but under ~$200/yr or otherwise hobbyist-reachable; circled-? marker); 'restricted' (no hobbyist path at any price — vetted partners, sector-only, no published rate; circled-? marker); 'weird' (something unusual that overrides the access question — non-standard NTRIP, active jamming/spoofing, infrastructure too sparse to work, war-disrupted; circled-? marker, note carries the warning). The tier drives marker style; whether station data exists is derived at runtime from stations.json (in-pipeline + data → coloured pins/circle; otherwise → grey circle for free, circled-? for the others).
_vrs_flag: Optional 'vrs': true means the network delivers VRS / network-RTK streams (a virtual reference station near the rover) rather than a single physical antenna. Orthogonal to tier — a network can be free+vrs (KSA-CORS, SAPOS), paid+vrs (swipos, HEPOS), restricted+vrs (DVRS, KazGeoDesy), etc. Absence of the flag means nothing — either the network is single-base, or VRS-status is unknown / not relevant. The flag is informational; the renderer uses it together with data presence to decide visuals (free+vrs+ingested → coloured ring; free+vrs+not-ingested → grey ring; non-VRS free entries with pins fall through to physical pins from stations.json).

markers.name: ReNEP
markers.note: 47 stations, free. Register at renep.dgterritorio.gov.pt; caster at 193.137.94.71 (ports 2101–2108).

markers.name: LitPOS
markers.note: 35 stations, free (publicly-funded EUPOS member). Host:port disclosed only after registration.

markers.name: ZAKPOS
markers.note: Nationwide network, hub at Mukachevo (western Ukraine). Paid; 15,000 UAH/yr (~$366/yr) wartime-reduced rate (April 2025). Pauses automatically during air-raid alerts.

markers.name: UA-System.NET
markers.note: Largest commercial network in Ukraine; 200+ stations, Leica VRS platform. Paid; regional packs (West/Karpaty/South/East) from ~13,000 UAH/yr (~$317/yr). Wartime discount plans for eastern and southern oblasts.

markers.name: RTK HUB
markers.note: Nationwide commercial RTK network (formerly TNT-TPI). Paid; 10,500 UAH/yr (~$256/yr). Host and port not published — disclosed after registration at rtkhub.com.

markers.name: GPSBru / AGN
markers.note: Single station at Uccle observatory, free. Port unconfirmed. Useful only within ~30 km of Brussels.

markers.name: UGRF CORS
markers.note: 78 stations, free as of 2024. Endpoint disclosed only after registration.

markers.name: ETCORS
markers.note: ~10 stations, intended free. Launched Dec 2025 by SSGI; NTRIP endpoint not yet publicly discoverable.

markers.name: DOL LandGNSS
markers.note: Free government service. Host:port not in public aggregators; the operator manual is in Thai.

markers.name: TPOS
markers.note: 11 stations, free. Self-service portal; no professional licence required. RTK, VRS/MAX/NRT mountpoints, and 1-year RINEX archive.

markers.name: STPOS
markers.note: 10 stations, free. SBC portal registration; ID + intended-use declaration required to activate RTK (RINEX available immediately). No professional restriction.

markers.name: Rete GNSS Veneto
markers.note: ~20 stations, free. Email to request credentials; open to any user. MAX3/IMAX/NRT mountpoints.

markers.name: Rete GNSS Liguria
markers.note: 10 stations, free. Online registration via regional geoportal. 7 Liguria stations + 3 shared with SPIN3 GNSS (northern border).

markers.name: Sicili@net
markers.note: ~80 stations (INGV Catania seismic network), free. Email to request credentials. MAX/IMAX (Leica), VRS (Trimble), FKP (Geo++) and RTCM 3.0 mountpoints.

markers.name: SARNET
markers.note: 14 stations, commercial network (SARNET s.r.l.). RTK, VRS, DGPS, and RINEX archive. Only documented correction source in Sardinia.

markers.name: ACORN
markers.note: Alaska state reference network (Alaska DOT/PF), intended free. NTRIP endpoint not confirmed from public sources.

markers.name: REMOS
markers.note: 27 NTRIP-capable stations under IGVSB, intended free. No public endpoint confirmed; operational status uncertain given infrastructure constraints.

markers.name: ROMPOS
markers.note: Under the cost of a capable base station. Monthly subscription also available.

markers.name: swipos
markers.note: At this price a local base station is likely more practical. Volunteer rtk2go/Centipede bases provide partial free coverage.

markers.name: CPOS / ETPOS
markers.note: Volunteer rtk2go/Centipede bases exist in populated areas (Oslofjord, Vestlandet).

markers.name: SIGNAL
markers.note: €622/yr (~$680/yr) early-discount tier available. Volunteer rtk2go/Centipede bases provide partial free coverage.

markers.name: SWEPOS Network RTK
markers.note: A free DGNSS tier exists but sub-metre only — out of scope for cm-grade work.

markers.name: SiReNT
markers.note: 3-day trial available but requires SingPass (Singapore residents only).

markers.name: MyRTKnet
markers.note: 78 stations under JUPEM (Survey Act cost-recovery). Pricing not published online.

markers.name: TUSAGA-Aktif
markers.yearly_cost: ₺550 (~$17) one-time device registration; ₺1,000/mo (~$30), ₺6,000/6 mo (~$182), or ₺8,135/yr (~$247) for RTK; ₺2,985/yr (~$91) for DGPS. KDV (VAT) included.
markers.note: Online registration requires a Turkish national ID (TC Kimlik No), so foreign visitors cannot self-register. Shorter blocks (₺1,000/mo, ₺6,000/6 mo, ~$30 / ~$182) are cheaper than committing to the annual ₺8,135 (~$247).

markers.name: VNGEONET
markers.yearly_cost: 750,000 VNĐ/mo (~$29.5), 4,280,000 VNĐ/6 mo (~$168), or 6,750,000 VNĐ/yr (~$266). Free 12-month RTK in zones with >80 km station spacing.
markers.note: 65 stations on a VRS + iMAX + single-base caster. Foreigners can register with a passport. A free annual tier exists in sparse-coverage zones (>80 km station spacing) — useful outside the densely covered river deltas.

markers.name: PAGeNet
markers.yearly_cost: PHP 1,000 (~$18) one-time registration; then PHP 100/hr (~$1.77/hr), or PHP 1,000/day (~$18), PHP 3,500/5 days, PHP 7,500/15 days, PHP 12,000/month (~$212) for unlimited RTK. No VAT — regulatory charges under Executive Order 471.
markers.note: 52 stations. The per-hour rate (~$1.77/hr) is cheap for occasional use; the 1-day pass (~$18) covers a single session, and the 1-month tier (~$212) is the longest published block. Non-Metro Manila clients pay by LandBank deposit slip, a practical barrier for foreigners.

markers.name: GNSSnet.hu
markers.yearly_cost: 150,000 HUF/yr (~€375, ~$415) for unlimited RTK or network RTK; 15,000 HUF (~€38) for 30 days within 50 km of one fixed point; or pay-per-minute at 8 HUF/min RTK and 12 HUF/min network RTK (~€1.20–1.80/hr). 12,000 HUF (~€30) one-time registration. Net of 27% Hungarian VAT.
markers.note: Annual subscription is over budget for a hobbyist, but a 30-day local-radius pass (~€38) or per-minute billing (~€1.20/hr) makes a single project affordable. Centipede has ~223 volunteer nodes in Hungary — a dense free alternative already on this map.

markers.name: AGROS
markers.note: Affordable RTK flat-rate. ~30 stations on a Trimble VRS Now backbone. Hourly and monthly packages also available.

markers.name: GeoNet GEO-RTK
markers.note: Bulgaria's national commercial network RTK / VRS service, certified by АГКК. Reach the caster at gnss.geonet.bg:2101. Tariff lives in a PDF on solitech.bg (April 2026 edition); contact info@geonet.bg or 0700 1 4677. No free hobbyist tier; access is contract-based.

markers.name: MONTEPOS
markers.note: 9 CORS stations. Seven subscription periods from 24 h to 2 years; EUR pricing on a 2024-04-11 PDF on wapi.gov.me. Host:port issued after registration. Admin contact Goran Popović, +382 67 641 119; payment to giro 832-1081-58.

markers.name: SRPOS
markers.yearly_cost: BAM/KM (pegged 1.95583 to 1 EUR). RTK: 0.20 KM/min, or 30 KM (~$17) for 10 hours, 50 KM (~$29) for 20 hours, 250 KM (~$145) for 1 month, 1,000 KM (~$578) for 1 year. DGPS 1 month 200 KM (~$116), 1 year 1,000 KM.
markers.note: Republika Srpska half of the BiHPOS network. ~17 stations, MAX + iMAX + VRS + FKP + nearest-station mountpoints. Short pre-paid blocks (10 hours ~$17, 20 hours ~$29) are the cheap end; per-minute (~$7/hr), 1-month (~$145), and the annual (~$578) climb steeply for any sustained use.

markers.name: FBiHPOS
markers.yearly_cost: BAM/KM (pegged 1.95583 to 1 EUR). 100 KM (~$58) one-time registration; then 150 KM (~$87) for 7 days, 250 KM (~$145) for 1 month, 750 KM (~$435) for 6 months, 1,000 KM (~$580) for 12 months. All services (RTK + post-processing) 12 months 1,400 KM. Multi-rover discounts -10% / -20% (max -50%).
markers.note: Federation of BiH half of the BiHPOS network. ~17 stations, MAX + iMAX + VRS + NEAREST + a combined H+V stream. Caster runs at fbihpos.katastar.ba on port 8080 (not the conventional 2101). Open to natural persons; the 7-day pass (~$87) is the cheapest short block, with longer tiers up to 1,000 KM (~$580) for 12 months.

markers.name: e-GNSS
markers.note: Pay-per-use only; registration is via paper form (mail or fax). Annual contracts available for regular users.

markers.name: CZEPOS
markers.note: Free only for education and government. No general hobbyist path.

markers.name: SKPOS
markers.yearly_cost: €70/yr (~$79) for unlimited RTK, or €25/mo (~$28); €140/yr for two simultaneous receivers; €25/yr for DGNSS. Includes 50 hours of RINEX. Free for Slovak public-sector bodies and municipalities.
markers.note: ~26 stations. One of the cheapest national network-RTK services in the EU. Registration explicitly accepts private individuals without a trade licence and is open to almost every country, so this is a practical paid path for Slovak and visiting hobbyists alike.

markers.name: SoI-CORS
markers.note: Free only for central/state government and academic institutions. The above rate is the private-user tariff.

markers.name: Réseau GNSS du Québec (MERN)
markers.note: 18 free government reference stations, but NOT standard NTRIP — each station delivers a raw TCP stream (per-station IP:port, CMR+/RTCM 3.2). Standard NTRIP clients will not connect; you need a TCP-capable receiver (e.g. Emlid RS2) or an RTKLIB str2str bridge.

markers.name: BC RTN
markers.note: No Canadian province offers free public NTRIP. Subscription portal currently unreachable (government website reorganisation); contact GeoBC to subscribe.

markers.name: Nova Scotia NSACS
markers.note: 40 government reference stations; real-time corrections only via paid commercial resellers (HxGN SmartNet, Can-Net, Brandtnet); no direct provincial caster. Price shown is HxGN SmartNet Atlantic plan — Can-Net and Brandtnet pricing not public.

markers.name: SCRTN
markers.note: No professional-licence requirement; any subscriber may obtain a login.

markers.name: WSRN
markers.note: PANGA/CWU contributes Puget Sound antennae and data archiving to this network.

markers.name: CRTN (SOPAC)
markers.note: ~250 reference stations via Scripps (UCSD); aggregates SCIGN, BARD, USGS Pasadena, Caltrans CVSRN, OCRTN, and EarthScope. Universities and schools are exempt from the fee. Significant station overlap with EarthScope (already on this map). Credentials take a week or more to issue.

markers.name: TxDOT CORS
markers.note: TxDOT employees and contractors only. No hobbyist registration path.

markers.name: CalRTNS
markers.note: Vetted state/county agency partners only. No public registration path.

markers.name: APN
markers.note: Government service (Survey of Israel), licensed surveyors only. WARNING: pervasive military GNSS spoofing across Israel and the surrounding region since Oct 2023 — RTK is unreliable regardless of NTRIP access.

markers.name: IGRS
markers.note: Iraq Geodetic Reference System has only 7 reference stations at 500–800 km spacing — far too sparse for RTK. No public NTRIP caster.

markers.name: Pak-Rehber
markers.note: Karachi metropolitan area only — not nationwide. Operated by SUPARCO Business Solutions. Explicitly restricted to authorised users; no public registration path.

markers.name: SLCORSnet
markers.note: Government network by the Survey Department; coverage mainly Western Province with island-wide rollout ongoing. Payment by bank transfer to Peoples Bank (Narahenpita) — may complicate non-resident registration.

markers.name: CORSnet
markers.note: Private island-wide network, founded 2014. Self-service registration open to individuals. Caster address provided post-registration.

markers.name: НЦГПИ / KazGeoDesy
markers.note: 120+ reference stations; self-service portal at rtk.qgeo.kz. Requires a Kazakh resident ID (ИИН or БИН) to register — foreign users cannot self-register. Baselines will be long outside Almaty and Astana.

markers.name: DVRS
markers.note: 18+ four-constellation stations under Dubai Municipality. Professional application required; no hobbyist registration path. Public portal unavailable as of 2026-04-30.

markers.name: REGPMOC
markers.note: ~65 single-base stations under IGN/Ministry of Defence. Access requires application + payment to IGN; no online self-service portal. IGN's policy does not explicitly exclude individuals, but there is no hobbyist-accessible sign-up path.

markers.name: EFT-CORS
markers.note: Hundreds of stations across Russia, multi-constellation. 3-day free trial; raw post-processing data is free.

markers.name: RTKNet
markers.note: 300+ stations nationwide; ports 6030–6041 by federal district. 3-day trial available.

markers.name: HIVE
markers.note: Pay-per-use: daily RTK or hourly post-processing. Station owners get free caster access in exchange for contributing data.

markers.name: ГЕОСПАЙДЕР
markers.note: 49 stations across NW Russia centred on St. Petersburg. Monthly, quarterly, and annual plans available.

markers.name: 千寻知寸 Qianxun
markers.note: 2,700+ stations across 33 provinces, multi-constellation. Individuals can register directly — no surveying licence required.

markers.name: 中国移动CORS
markers.note: 4,400+ stations nationwide via China Mobile — the largest of the three commercial options. Individual registration available.

markers.name: Tencent RTK
markers.note: ~2,800+ virtual stations across 33 provinces. WeChat or QQ account required; no surveying licence. Current pricing unconfirmed beyond the 2022 launch figure.

markers.name: KOPOS
markers.note: 8 CORS stations, VRS network. One-time €20 registration fee also applies. NTRIP credentials issued inside the online portal after account creation.

markers.name: OTC GNSS
markers.note: 23 physical stations, non-Saharan Tunisia. Shorter durations available from 60 TND/day (~$21). Prices exclude VAT. No explicit eligibility restriction stated.
